attacks.claim: The nightly job scores all 340k recipes per pantry user in one SQL statement on the primary. Staging tested 12,000 users in 41 minutes, but sizing assumes ~630k pantry users (~52x). Linear extrapolation is ~35 hours, far beyond any nightly window, and it would hammer the single primary that serves production writes for a 2.1M MAU app. No replica use, chunking, or incremental scoring is planned.
attacks.evidence: "score every recipe in the catalog (340k recipes) in a single SQL statement joining pantry_items x recipe_ingredients on the primary" / "Staging run: 12,000 synthetic pantry users completed in 41 minutes." / "30% of MAU create a pantry within 90 days"

attacks.claim: The top churn reason is too much setup/typing (38%), yet the plan gates all value behind manually entering 15 items with quantity, unit, and expiry via a form. There is no bulk entry, staples quick-pick, or scan, and no evidence users will reach the threshold. The plan worsens the leading failure mode and risks near-zero unlock.
attacks.evidence: "unlocks once a user has entered at least 15 items with expiry dates" / "Users add items with a form: ingredient (autocomplete...), quantity, unit, expiry date."

attacks.claim: The adoption and success targets are unsupported and inconsistent: 30% create a pantry in 90 days (sizing) versus 25% unlock (15 dated items) in 60 days. There is no prototype or offline match-quality check showing a 15-item pantry yields usable recipes. The retention metric has no control-matching method for a self-selected population.
attacks.evidence: "25% of MAU unlock Pantry Match within 60 days" vs "30% of MAU create a pantry within 90 days"; "+3 pts 30-day retention for users who unlock vs. matched control"

attacks.claim: There is no timeout, retry, idempotency, failure alerting, or freshness/observability for PantryMatchJob or pushes. A mid-run failure leaves pantry_matches stale or partial and goes undetected. Matches are also only refreshed nightly, so edits to the pantry leave the carousel and expiry alerts stale.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: timeout, retry, failure alerting, or staleness monitoring for PantryMatchJob; "PantryMatchJob (Sidekiq, nightly 02:00 UTC)"

attacks.claim: The plan has no feature flag, kill switch, or rollback path for the new tab, carousel, nightly job, or push notifications. The rollout goes 5% then 100% in the final week with no load-test gate or rollback criteria.
attacks.evidence: "Week 6: beta to 5% of users, then 100%." / ABSENT: feature flag, kill switch, or rollback plan

attacks.claim: The plan collects per-user pantry contents, quantities, and expiry dates, and persists match rows, with no retention, deletion, or account-deletion cascade defined. Analytics events are also unspecified.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: retention/deletion policy for pantry_items and pantry_matches; "Week 5: notifications, analytics events."

attacks.claim: The scoring spec is underspecified. The gate requires expiry dates, but the plan doesn't define how expiry weighting combines with coverage, how ties and the top-50 cutoff work, or what happens with expired items. Quantities and units are collected and prompted for, but the score is presence-only, so the quantity prompt has no defined effect.
attacks.evidence: "Score = (pantry ingredients used / recipe ingredients) weighted by expiry proximity" vs "Users are asked to update quantities after cooking"

attacks.claim: No compute or database cost estimate is given for the nightly job or table growth.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: compute or DB cost estimate for PantryMatchJob or pantry_matches

attacks.claim: Quiet-hours enforcement doesn't say how local time is determined or what happens when the timezone is unknown.
No accessibility requirements are specified for the progress bar, autocomplete, or expiry indicators.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: accessibility requirements for progress bar and expiry indicators
